Parsed per <tr> block inside the table.tier-list container: the letter from the row's first <td>, the spec from each tier-list-entry's FIRST img alt looked up WHOLE against the roster rather than split positionally ("Vengeance Demon Hunter" splits to class "Hunter"). Counts reconciled and printed per page BEFORE the merge: raid 27 DPS / 7 healer / 6 tank = 40, M+ 27 / 7 / 6 = 40, 120 rows, 0 unmatched. Each page's JSON-LD dateModified was re-read live rather than carried forward and is unchanged, matching this run's pre-agent published-evidence artifact exactly: raid DPS 2026-08-30, raid healer 2026-09-01, raid tank 2026-08-29, M+ DPS/healer/tank all 2026-08-30. Both JSON API files fetched this run with plain curl, no headers, no proxy, no auth; the web page was deliberately not touched (it is a stale S3 prerender). manifest.json returned completedAt 2026-09-08T14:03:05Z and snapshotDate 2026-09-08, and rankings/midnight/mplus/all/0.json returned 162,405 bytes with Last-Modified: Tue, 08 Sep 2026 09:11:42 GMT — manifest and payload agree, so this is not the 2026-08-04 pinned-manifest shape. The rankings file is 44 blocks; selecting categoryType in {dps, hps, tank} AND sortField "lowerBound" AND keyRange undefined (whitelisting the three types, because melee and ranged are subsets of dps and would double-count 27 specs) yielded exactly 27 + 7 + 6 = 40 rows, 0 unmatched against the roster. The payload was DIFFED rather than trusted to the manifest date: all 40 lowerBound values round-trip byte-identical to the stored rows at 1 dp, so upstream has not re-run since last night and there was nothing to merge — no apply-metrics call was made and no stored value or date was touched. The stored coverage date stays the source-published 2026-09-08 (never today), which is one day old and inside the success cross-check.

Recorded from this run's pre-agent wcl-fetch/evidence.json legacy block (attemptedAt 2026-09-09T14:47:01Z), which reports status unreachable: exact live raid population medians still have no verified sanctioned aggregate endpoint. I hold no WCL credentials and made no warcraftlogs.com request of any kind. The 47 stored rows ("Median rDPS (Mythic, all bosses)" 27, its tank cut 6, "Median HPS (Mythic, all bosses)" 7, "Median DPS (Mythic, healer)" 7) keep their 2026-08-10 dates and values untouched. Two standing corrections restated because they are easy to re-derive wrongly: rdps is defined FFXIV-only in the official schema, so its rejection is not a WoW outage diagnostic, and this run's supported WoW dps/hps collection succeeded on both brackets — the new per-encounter top-100-entry leaderboard series is a DIFFERENT quantity and cannot green this aggregate requirement.

Recorded from the same pre-agent wcl-fetch/evidence.json legacy block: same finding as wcl-live-raid — no verified sanctioned aggregate endpoint for exact live M+ population medians, and public statistics pages return verification challenges. The trusted pre-agent collector (src/fetch-stable-metrics.mjs, checkedAt 2026-09-09T14:49:17Z) reports status success for all three meta pages — DPS 71,302 / healer 42,311 / tank 40,911 bytes, HTTP 200, 1 attempt each — with 40 rows, roleCounts 27/7/6 and 0 omitted specs. I merged ONLY metrics-fetch/updates.json through src/apply-metrics.mjs and did not re-parse murlok.io myself. PARTIAL, not success, because the source's own date has not moved: every page's <time datetime> still reads 2026-09-02 (dateBasis source-time-datetime), all 40 stored values are unchanged, and the collector correctly kept that source-owned asOf rather than stamping the fetch date — so the stored coverage date is 7 days old against a 5-day threshold and the age heartbeat should go red. That red is the honest signal that Murlok has not recomputed, not a fetch failure. node src/check-stable-metrics.mjs passes.

All 27 DPS specs requested fresh this run at talent_target_scaling/castingpatchwerk with up to 3 attempts each. 23 charts returned HTTP 200 with real data; the same persistent 4 (Balance Druid, Feral Druid, Augmentation Evoker, Devastation Evoker) returned the 76-byte {"status": "error"} body on every attempt, which is the documented upstream not-re-simmed state rather than a transport failure, and they hold no stored profile to lose. simc_settings.ptr was compared explicitly against the string "0" (truthy in JS) on every chart, and simc_settings.tier was READ off each chart rather than assumed: all 23 carry tier MID2, matching the stored pool exactly, so the pool stays tier-uniform at 23 profiles and no partial-merge hazard arises. Targets were taken from data["MID2"][count] (already best-build) for counts 1/2/3/5/8/15. Upstream re-simmed today: every chart's own timestamp reads 2026-09-09, so asOf is the CHART's date per spec and not the run date — the coverage date moves because upstream moved. Pre-merge diff across the 138 overlapping target rows: 0 moved more than 60%, so no value_move_ack is needed; row count held at 23, well above the floor of 15 and outside maxRowDropPct.

MID2_Raid.txt fetched fresh (HTTP 200, 1,368,993 bytes) and it HAS a "DPS Ranking:" block this run, so the plain-text lane was used and the HTML fallback was not needed. Era-verified off the header build string, not the visible version: "SimulationCraft 1210-01 for World of Warcraft 12.1.0.69587 Live (hotfix 2026-09-08/69587, git build HEAD ba72a9dcfe, no-networking)" — the HEAD hash moved from f5b50a3f97 to ba72a9dcfe, which is the honest explanation for the values moving. 43 profiles parsed, the leading Raid aggregate row skipped, mapped by LONGEST-PREFIX with a hyphen allowed in the hero-variant suffix (so MID2_Death_Knight_Frost_Rider and MID2_Demon_Hunter_Havoc_Fel-Scarred both resolve) and reduced to the best hero variant per spec: 23 of 27 DPS specs, with the 7 tank profiles correctly unmapped and Balance, Feral, Augmentation and Devastation absent upstream exactly as under the 2026-09-03 MID2 adoption. All 23 rows moved on the new build and none moved more than 60%, so no ack is needed; row count holds at 23 against a floor of 15.

The trusted pre-agent collector reports status success: https://mythicstats.com/period/latest resolved to /period/1080 (last night was 1079, so the weekly period rolled), HTTP 200, 265,989 bytes, 40 rows with roleCounts 27/7/6 and 0 omitted specs. I merged ONLY metrics-fetch/updates.json and did not re-parse the site. The receipt's shape checks hold and are the only thing distinguishing this share column from the /meta per-key-presence column: role subtotals Ranged 35.9 / Melee 23.9 / Tank 20.1 / Healer 20.2, total 100.1. All 44 unique tracked YouTube channels polled inline via the public RSS feed endpoint — 41 class creators plus the 3 generalCreators — 15 entries each, 660 entries, 0 fetch failures. media:description parsed alongside the title on every entry. The seen-set was recomputed as the union of the four structured lanes (pending seen[]/skipped[]/videos[] plus every youtu.be id in a take or metaNote url), 1,249 ids, never by regex over log prose; 314 unseen videos fall on or after the cycle-opening build date 2026-06-18, derived as the OLDEST date in ptr-builds.json rather than by index. This is a NIGHTLY, so the queue stayed keyword-filtered. All 7 videos the deterministic Supadata step delivered (transcript-fetch/summary.json verdict "ok": 3 fetched, 4 cached, usage 11 counted requests in a 30-day window) were read in full and resolved: 2 distilled, 5 verified-skipped, queue drained to 0 and then 1 new video queued.
